sentence: This project uses medical imaging techniques to measure aortic pressure and wall stiffness in patients with aortic dissection.
This project studies how cancer cells use a protein-lipid immune checkpoint to evade the immune system and whether blocking it helps immune cells control cancer.
This project studies how the autophagy pathway affects artery calcification and tries to find the molecules in that pathway involved.
This project develops a combination vaccine against enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli and Shigella, using a multiepitope fusion antigen platform and animal challenge models.
This project uses pluripotent stem cells to build models of human somite formation and limb development and studies how body patterns form.
This project tries to find the genetic variations that cause Inflammatory Bowel Disease, a chronic disorder that includes Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis.
This project tries to find out what causes phosphorylation of protective proteins in synucleinopathies and how it changes the protein networks they interact with.
This project studies how neutralizing antibodies bind to HIV and how that relates to their breadth and efficacy of action.
This project studies how somatic and germline changes work together to cause clear cell renal cell carcinoma, using computational, functional, and clinical approaches.
This project builds laboratory tests and software that predict which cancer-specific markers called neoantigens are likely to activate the immune system.
This project tries to find out how henipaviruses manipulate regulatory pathways to enhance infection.
This project looks for neural circuits linking the spinal cord dorsal horn and brainstem that process visceral interoceptive signals from the mouse colon.
This project uses induced pluripotent stem cell derived endothelial cells to study how genetic markers affect vascular health in African American cigarette and e-cigarette users.
This project uses genomic and epigenomic techniques in families and unrelated cases to find the molecular cause of otosclerosis, a disorder of abnormal bone remodeling.
This project studies how a deficiency disrupts bile acid metabolism and triggers adaptive stress responses in liver cells made from patient-specific cells.
This project studies how bitter taste receptors in nasal ciliated and tuft cells control host defense and inflammation in chronic rhinosinusitis, using mouse models.
This project tries to find the transcription factors that control axon growth in retinal ganglion cells and tests them in an optic nerve regeneration model.
This project studies how the sex-steroid hormone estradiol controls gene expression in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
This project uses a high-throughput approach to study what multiple genes linked to autism spectrum disorders do in the developing brain.
This project studies pH based visualization and modulation of infiltrative tumor cells in glioblastoma, aiming to target them.
